messages.subject: Legend display with two dataframes
parts:
Hello there,

I have a plot like the one below where I have raw data points displayed as small grey points and some summary statistics displayed as larger black points. These figures display beautifully using ggplot2. The only issue is in the legend. Running the example below illustrates that one of the points (unfilled diamond) doesn't look quite right in the legend. The smaller grey point is being displayed inside the larger point. I imagine that this is happening also in the filled points, but that the grey point is just not visible.

Can anyone recommend a way to remove the grey points from the legend while retaining the black filled points?

Thanks in advance.

Sam

#Some data
dat <- data.frame(x = runif(270, 0, 125), z = rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 3),
 yy = letters[1:3], stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

#mean and statistic
summ <- ddply(dat, .(z, yy), summarise, m = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
#plot
ggplot(data = summ, aes(x = yy, y = x)) +
    geom_point(data=summ, aes(group=z,shape = z), size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    geom_errorbar(data=summ,aes(ymin = m - sd, ymax = m + sd), width = 0.5, size = 0.5,  position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    geom_point(data=dat, aes(x= yy, y=x, shape=z, group=z), alpha=0.4,position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    scale_shape_manual(value=c(19,5,17))

messages.author: b3ca0c52e87f982f
messages.subject: Re: Legend display with two dataframes
parts:
Hi Sam,

you can just use the option legend=FALSE into the geom_point call you
don't want to appear in the legend.

Best,

Matthieu

Matthieu Dubois
Post-doctoral Fellow
National Fund for Scientific Research (Belgium)
